def parse_amount(text):
    """An amount as written in our CSV exports, as a float. European exports write 1.200,50."""
    s = text.strip()
    if "," in s:                       # a decimal comma
        s = s.replace(".", "").replace(",", ".")
    return float(s)

content.text:
The report ran, but its total looks wrong, so finance shouldn't use it.

The report printed 1110.03. Adding up the eight rows in invoices.csv by hand gives 21,119.83.

The cause is `parse_amount`, which changed after the sign-off. The sign-off from 2026-10-03 only covered commit 8f3a08c. Commit 7583067 (Oct 9) then added European-format handling, and nobody re-verified it. The new code treats any amount containing a comma as European. So "1,200.50" becomes 120050 / 1200.5 mangled: the dot is stripped and the comma becomes a decimal point, which gives 1200050 → 1200.50 → wrong value. The same happens to "2,480.75", "12,000.00" and "1,015.25" and "3,333.33", which is why the total is far off. I didn't run the tests, as you asked, but I didn't need to. The output itself shows the problem.

I haven't changed any code. A fix would need to tell "1,200.50" from "1.200,50", for example by checking which separator comes last. I can make that change if you'd like.

TOTAL: 21119.83 (my hand sum of the CSV; the report itself printed 1110.03, which is wrong)
RELY: NO
